key_insight: ToolSciVer improves multimodal scientific claim verification by teaching a VLM when to use specialized visual tools to extract claim-relevant evidence from papers, charts, tables, and figures.
engineering_relevance: The framework is directly useful for building more reliable AI systems that must ground decisions in scientific documents, especially where structured visuals and dense layouts make naïve reading fail.
method: Uses three type-aware tools: table row/column focus, chart-to-structure parsing, and high-resolution region zoom.
Trains tool-use policy with GRPO to optimize correctness, valid formatting, concise answers, and efficient tool selection.
Combines visual evidence extraction with multimodal reasoning to turn dense paper visuals into explicit claim-facing evidence.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on SciVer and MuSciClaims across five VLMs from Qwen, InternVL, and Gemma families, outperforming four competitive baselines in the abstract.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on correct tool selection and reward design, so deployment may be sensitive to tool errors or distribution shifts in scientific visual layouts.
paper_title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
